newsitem.title: USA: Navistar sees drop in heavy truck demand.
newsitem.headline: Navistar sees drop in heavy truck demand.

text.p: Navistar International Corp said Thursday it expects industry demand for heavy trucks in the United States and Canada to fall to 180,000 units in fiscal 1997 from 195,400 sold in 1996.

"However, given recent indications of continued strength in the truck market, there may be upside beyond our current forecast," said John Horne, Navistar's chairman and chief executive, in a statement.
The company also said it expects that industry demand for medium trucks in the United States and Canada will decline to 112,000 units in 1997 from 113,200 trucks sold in 1996.
Navistar also forecast industry demand for school buses in fiscal 1997 will fall slightly below the 32,500 buses sold in 1996.
Earlier, Navistar said it earned $30 million, or $0.31 a share, in the second quarter ended April, versus $26 million, or $0.26 a share, a year ago.

The company said shipments to date are consistent with a year ago. But it plans to raise production schedules to better position the company in light of the indications for demand in the truck market to be stronger than originally expected.
"Our engine business, in particular, is showing real strength due to rising customer orders," Horne said.

In the third quarter, Navistar plans to raise production schedules at its Springfield, Ohio, truck assembly plant with production of its medium truck and school bus line increasing from 266 to 284 units a day. Heavy truck production will be held at 65 units per day, it said. Heavy duty truck production was increased at its Chatham, Ontario, truck plant from 62 to 100 units a day in late April.
Engine production is also expected to increase at the company's Indianapolis, Ind., plant as individual bottlenecks are eliminated, Navistar said.
